report.body:
Military Police in Água Clara, Mato Grosso do Sul, were told on Wednesday 4
November 2026 that a man was selling drugs from a white Volkswagen Gol in the
Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. The driver tried to flee when officers
approached and was stopped after a chase of several blocks. In the car they
found a portion of a substance similar to cocaine. At his home they seized
three portions of marijuana totalling about 20 grams, a precision scale and
material for packaging drugs. The man, identified as L.E.A., aged 30, was
taken to the Civil Police station and was already under investigation by the
General Investigations Section.

Civil Police, with Military Police support, found 59 tablets of marijuana
weighing about 54 kilograms at a second property used to store drugs. Two
men, A.A.S., aged 18, and J.V.M.C., aged 20, were arrested in flagrante at that
address.

The work continued into Thursday 5 November, when officers seized about 500
grams of marijuana and another precision scale from M.V.S.S., aged 22. They
also found a bag with 120 grams of cocaine in 19 portions, which they said the
first suspect had discarded during the Military Police stop. Police counted
marijuana and cocaine together in a combined seizure of about 54.64 kilograms. The same day Civil Police captured W.R.C., aged 28, who was under
investigation for drug trafficking and had an open arrest warrant.

Four of the men were arrested in flagrante for drug trafficking and association
for trafficking, and the fifth was held on the existing warrant. Police
also seized a car, a motorcycle, three precision scales, three mobile phones,
packaging and about R$250. A later account gave that combined drug weight
as 54 kilograms and 640 grams of marijuana and cocaine.

The Sohag Criminal Court, presided over by Judge Hamdi Abdel Aziz, sentenced
three people to death by hanging for possessing hashish with intent to traffic
and for possessing a scalpel without legal justification in the Maragha district
of Sohag, and ordered them to pay costs and the confiscation of what was seized. The public prosecution investigated, put the charges in the case papers to
the three, and referred them to the Sohag Criminal Court for trial.

Sada El Balad identified the defendants as M. A., 35, a technical-school diploma
holder; M. M., 25, also a technical-school diploma holder; and A. A., 41, who
was unemployed. The case dates to November 2025, when investigations
accused the three of possessing drugs in Maragha with intent to traffic and
promote them, and of possessing a cutting tool without legal justification.
Ahl Masr named the three as Mohamed Ismail Abdallah Mohamed, Mohamed Mohamed
Farghali Ahmed and Essam Ismail Abdallah Mohamed, all from Al-Ghanayem in
Assiut, and said they were accused of drug trafficking in the referral order. Officers of the Anti-Narcotics General Administration for Middle Upper
Egypt, Sohag branch, arrested the defendants after a prosecution warrant to
search the first of them, in case 16693 of 2025, Maragha felonies, also
registered as 3346 of 2025 at North Sohag.

A chemical laboratory report found the seized brown material was hashish, in
three lots of 80, 150 and 50 pieces, 280 pieces in all, plus a plastic sack with
traces of the drug. The prosecution charged the three with possessing
hashish with intent to traffic and with using cars to transport and promote the
drugs outside the cases permitted by law. Ahl Masr said the court referred
the papers to the Grand Mufti for a religious opinion on hanging the three, and
after that opinion returned sentenced them to death by hanging unanimously.
Ahl Masr said the Mufti approved the death sentences and that the court then
issued what it called a final judgment of death by hanging, by unanimous opinion
of the bench.

report.body:
Officers of the Mossos d'Esquadra criminal investigation division arrested seven
men, aged 29 to 55, on 1 October 2026 at an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, in
the Alt Empordà, Girona. The men were suspected of belonging to a group
dedicated to drug trafficking. Inside the warehouse officers found the
seven unloading pallets from an articulated truck so the hashish could be moved
into vans for later distribution. The narcotics group of the DIC in Sant
Feliu de Llobregat led the investigation, and officers of the ARRO in Girona
supported the entry.

Agents seized 8,025 kilograms of hashish hidden among the cargo, inside large
raffia sacks filled with rubber crumb, a method used to hinder detection at
police or customs checks. Mossos valued the seized hashish at more than
16.2 million euros on the illicit market. During the search officers found
a firearm in one of the detainees' vans. The inquiry began in June 2026
after Mossos intercepted a van in Viladecans carrying about 2,400 kilograms of
hashish, later linked to the Cabanes warehouse; that earlier quantity is not
part of the 8,025 kilograms seized on 1 October. The warehouse was almost
entirely open and had no sign of a business or of anyone living there, which
Mossos took as confirmation that it was used only as a logistics base for drug
trafficking.

The seven were brought before the civil and investigating section of the
Instance Court in Figueres, and the investigation remained open. The High
Court of Justice of Catalonia said the Figueres court ordered communicated
provisional detention without bail for four of the men, described as the main
figures, and provisional detention with bail for the other three, for offences
against public health and criminal organisation. Mossos were still looking
for two further members of the group, the truck driver and one of the leaders.

report.title: Ceuta truck driver remanded over hashish hidden in port truck
report.summary: A judge ordered preventive prison for the truck driver UDYCO arrested at the port of Ceuta with hashish hidden in a false bottom. Earlier reports estimated the haul at about 300 kilograms, while police had given no official weight.
report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. The hashish was hidden in a double bottom at the rear of the cab and at the end of the cargo area, and the truck was heading for the boarding zone with no cargo other than the drug. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure. Officers broke open the well-made double bottom with hammers, shears, mallets and an angle grinder.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday the judicial authority ordered the driver into preventive prison for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open over suspicions of larger loads and of heavy vehicles concealed in hashish stash sites.

report.title: Five held in Palma as police put the hashish seizure at 60 kg
report.summary: National Police said they arrested four men and a woman in Palma and seized 60 kilos of hashish, 24 kilos from a parcel and 36 kilos from a home, plus about 10,000 euros and weapons. A second home search also found two kilos of cocaine, which is not counted as cannabis, and the investigation remains open.
report.body:
Officers of the National Police's Drugs and Organised Crime Unit (Udyco)
arrested at least three people on Mallorca who were storing almost 50 kilos of
hashish for sale. The suspects received the hashish from the Spanish
mainland in courier parcels, according to the newspaper's case sources. The
arrests took place on Wednesday 4 November. Officers searched a home in
Marratxí, a municipality east of Palma, and another in a town in es Raiguer, the
district around the town of Inca. An investigating court in Palma declared
the case secret. Investigators had followed the suspects for some time;
over the previous months they had collected parcels of the drug from courier
companies and kept them at home for sale through others in the network.

In the Marratxí search, police found a large quantity of hashish in a chest
freezer and an air rifle. A woman was arrested there over her alleged link
to the criminal organisation and was released at the police station hours later. Two more people were arrested the same day, and all the suspects are
Spanish nationals.

The investigation is still open, further arrests are not ruled out, and the
suspects were due to appear before a Palma court in the coming hours. Ultima Hora said the five were accused of an offence against public health and of belonging to a criminal group. A further person was arrested in connection with the case; police suspect the drugs were supplied to others for smaller-scale sale, and the investigation remains open. In a second home officers arrested a man suspected of storing and transporting drugs and found two kilos of cocaine, further doses, cutting agent, a pistol with 9 mm cartridges, a bow and arrows, and a hydraulic press they said was for compressing cocaine. Ultima Hora said the man and his partner were detained after that search. In the main suspect's home officers found 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with a silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash, and arrested the man and a woman for drug trafficking and belonging to a criminal group or organisation. Officers intercepted a parcel addressed to a man living in Palma that contained 24 kilos of hashish and arrested him for a possible drug-trafficking offence. Ultima Hora identified the unit as Grupo I of the Drugs and Organised Crime Unit, Udyco. Grupo I de Estupefacientes said the investigation had begun months earlier and ended with five people detained. National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma on suspicion of belonging to a drug-trafficking group and seized 60 kilos of hashish and weapons.

the Asir region after they were convicted of jointly smuggling hashish into the
kingdom. The ministry named the three as Seni Redi Aqous Qorzqor, Shanafi

sentenced them to death as a discretionary punishment. The ruling was
upheld on appeal and confirmed by the Supreme Court, and a royal order was

October 2026, in the Asir region. The ministry said the announcement
affirmed the Saudi government's commitment to protecting citizens and residents
from the scourge of drugs and to imposing the strictest penalties prescribed by

report.body:
Immigration police, with officials from the Department of Thai Traditional and
Alternative Medicine, searched a three-storey luxury rental house in Soi Khu Bon
27, Yaek 14, Tha Raeng, Bang Khen, Bangkok, at 13:00 on 19 October 2026.
The search was under Minburi Criminal Court warrant K.428/2569, issued that day,
after neighbours complained about a strong cannabis smell. Officers
arrested one Vietnamese national and four workers from Myanmar who were sorting
cannabis buds for packing and delivery to customers.

Black bags of cannabis buds were found on all three floors, and the seizure was
more than five tonnes. Police also described the same seizure as five
tonnes of cannabis buds. The house had a ventilation system installed to
push the smell outside. The four Myanmar workers were paid about 200 to 300
baht a day, and police suspected the Vietnamese man was supervising the work. A Thai person had signed the lease before the foreigners moved in, and they
had lived and worked there for more than a year. Officers had spent about
two months gathering evidence before moving in.

A legal officer of the Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine
said selling or processing cannabis buds requires a licence for the place of
operation. The licence found was issued in Nong Bua Lamphu province and did
not cover Bangkok, an offence carrying up to one year in prison or a fine of up
to 20,000 baht. The seized buds were to be sent for laboratory tests to see
whether they were grown in Thailand or imported, and police were still tracing
the Thai tenant and others behind the operation.

A court in Mykolaiv sentenced a 51-year-old resident to nine years in prison for
growing cannabis at his home and storing dried narcotic material for sale.
Officers of police station No. 2 of the Mykolaiv district police department
uncovered his activity in July 2026. The first-instance verdict has not
entered into legal force.

Mykolaiv Oblast Prosecutor's Office said the July search of his house found 14
cannabis plants and more than eight kilograms of cannabis. He grew the
plants on his household plot, fertilising the soil, clearing weeds and watering
them regularly. The prosecutor's office said the growing had gone on since
April 2026. He dried part of the harvest in the attic and ground and packed
another part in glass jars for storage and, investigators said, for sale.

Police detained him under Article 208 of the Criminal Procedure Code and
notified him of suspicion under Part 3 of Article 307, for illegal production,
manufacture, acquisition, storage for sale and sale of narcotics in especially
large amounts, and under Part 1 of Article 310, for sowing or growing cannabis. At trial he partly admitted guilt, the prosecutor's office said. The
court found him guilty of growing cannabis and of making and storing drugs for
sale in especially large amounts. All of the seized narcotic material was
sent for expert examination.
